haiku-low.q1: It returns 202 with accepted count and a rejected list (index, event_id, reason), only after every accepted event is appended and acknowledged by all replicas.
haiku-low.q2: A 4xx is never retried. A 429 or 503 means back off from 1 s up to 5 minutes, then resend the whole batch. Timeouts are NOT STATED specifically.
haiku-low.q3: The first copy received wins. The later copy is dropped as a duplicate by the live job's claim on event_id.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday. dt is the UTC date of received_at, so it goes in Tuesday's partition and is replayed with Tuesday.
haiku-low.q5: In the key-value store, keyed event:<event_id>, value (partition, offset), with an 8-day TTL that removes old entries automatically.
haiku-low.q6: The live job stops reading and lag builds. No duplicates pass and no events are dropped. Collector behavior during that outage is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q7: Offsets are committed only after the warehouse write succeeds. On redelivery the claim matches, and insert-if-absent on (dt, event_id) adds no duplicate rows.
haiku-low.q8: Input is the raw archive in object storage. Rebuilt events are written to a hidden stage table, then atomically swapped into events_clean for that day.
haiku-low.q9: It keeps a copy only if no copy of that event_id has a lower log offset in day D or the 8 prior days, read from the archive.
haiku-low.q10: If it fails before publish, events_clean for D stays as live left it. The lock is released or left for the operator, who fixes and reruns, or releases the lock after confirming the run is dead.
haiku-low.q11: Only sealed closed days whose raw data exists for D and the 8 prior days, roughly up to 82 days old.
haiku-low.q12: Not decided. The hook currently passes every event through unchanged. Product must decide whether to drop or flag bots and set the detection rule and owner.

sonnet.q1: It accepts the valid events and rejects the malformed ones (missing event_id/device_id, or over 32 KB). Rejected events are not stored. The rest are stamped and appended to the log with all-replica acknowledgement. It returns 202 with {accepted: n, rejected: [{index, event_id if present, reason}]} only after every append is acknowledged by all replicas. (An unparseable or over-100-event batch gets a 4xx {error}.)
sonnet.q2: On a 429/503 (log down, slow or shedding load), the client backs off from 1 s up to 5 minutes and resends the whole batch. Resending is safe because dedup is by event_id. A 4xx is not retried. A timeout is not described explicitly; the collector keeps no state, so a failed request can simply be sent again.
sonnet.q3: The first copy received (the one with the lower log offset, all copies being on one log partition) wins and is the one in events_clean. The later copy is dropped. The live dedup claim lasts 8 days (7-day retry window plus 1 day).
sonnet.q4: Tuesday. Only received_at (collector server time, UTC) decides the day, so dt is Tuesday's date and it belongs to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay. The client timestamp is not used.
sonnet.q5: In the key-value store. For each event_id it holds the key event:<event_id> with value (partition, offset) of the winning record, set only if absent (atomic claim). Entries are removed by an 8-day per-key TTL.
sonnet.q6: The live job stops reading and lag builds. No duplicates pass and no events are dropped. The collector keeps accepting events into the log (the collector and archiver do not depend on the KV store), and the live job catches up when the store returns. Freshness and lag alerts fire.
sonnet.q7: Offsets are committed only after the warehouse write succeeds, so a crash means the records are redelivered (not lost). On redelivery, the KV claim finds a stored value equal to this record's (partition, offset), so it is recognized as the winner and goes on. The warehouse insert is insert-if-absent on (dt, event_id), so the retry adds nothing a second time (no double-counting).
sonnet.q8: It reads only the raw archive in object storage (of a sealed day D, plus the 8 days before it for dedup), not the log or the KV store. Rebuilt events are written to a hidden stage table such as events_clean_stage_<D>_<run_id>, which dashboards cannot see.
sonnet.q9: It drops overlapping archive records by (log_partition, log_offset). It keeps a copy of an event in D only if no copy with the same event_id has a lower offset, either in D or in the 8 days before it (read from the archive). Since all copies of an event are on one log partition, earlier means lower offset. The live job uses the same rule, so both pick the same copy.
sonnet.q10: Nothing is published: events_clean for D stays as live left it (old day intact; the swap is atomic, so no half-built day). The stage is kept for inspection (a validation failure) or dropped by the next run. On normal end the lock is deleted; if the job crashed, the lock stays and the operator confirms the run is dead and runs replay --day D --release. Then the operator fixes the cause and re-runs, or for a validation failure re-runs with a named override giving the failed check and a reason. Re-running is safe.
sonnet.q11: Only closed days (D closes at 02:00 UTC on D+1) that are sealed (sealed/dt=D exists), have no stale/dt=D marker, have no replay already running, and have raw data for D and the 8 days before it. That limits replay to days up to about 82 days old (90-day archive minus 8). Enrichment versions must also be pinned.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Currently a hook exists but passes every event through unchanged. Product must still decide whether suspected bots are dropped or kept with an is_suspected_bot column, and the detection rule and its owner. The hook never changes which copy wins. The archive keeps everything, so a replay can apply the decision later.
